not_covered: Callers outside this repository (none tracked in the repo)

requirements: R1: save_cache(path, entries) writes the JSON object {"version": 2, "entries": entries}; load_cache(path) returns the entries of a version-2 file and {} for a missing, unreadable, or older-format file.
R2: MAX_ATTEMPTS becomes 5, and should_retry(attempts_made) returns True exactly when attempts_made < MAX_ATTEMPTS, so a sync is attempted at most MAX_ATTEMPTS times in total.
R3: clear_cache(user, path) deletes the cache file only when user.is_admin is True; for any other user it raises PermissionError and leaves the file in place.
risks: cache file format (persisted state): low, because the cache is local and regenerable and a bad file only causes a cache miss
retry counter (inclusive/exclusive boundary): low, because an off-by-one costs at most one background attempt more or less
clear_cache admin-only check (authorization; public signature change): medium, because unauthorized clearing forces a cache rebuild
invariants: I1: a non-admin clear_cache never removes the file (denial fails closed)
I2: load_cache never raises for a missing, unreadable, or old-format file
I3: should_retry(n) is True iff n < MAX_ATTEMPTS
preserved_behaviors: P1: load_cache returns {} on OSError or invalid JSON
P2: clear_cache by an admin on a missing file is a no-op
P3: a save_cache/load_cache round-trip returns the saved entries

findings.claim: clear_cache raises AttributeError, not PermissionError, when the user object has no is_admin attribute or is None
evidence: probe: SimpleNamespace() and None -> AttributeError, file still exists
findings.failure_mechanism: principal without is_admin -> AttributeError before os.remove -> file kept (fails closed); a caller that catches only PermissionError sees a different exception
findings.severity_change_reason: The contract defines a user by user.is_admin; an object without that attribute (or None) is an input the contract excludes, and denial still fails closed, so I1 holds
findings.rejection_reason: The contract defines a user by user.is_admin; an object without that attribute (or None) is an input the contract excludes, and denial still fails closed, so I1 holds

findings.claim: clear_cache raises AttributeError, not PermissionError, for a user object without is_admin or user=None
evidence: probe: object without is_admin -> AttributeError, file exists True
findings.failure_mechanism: anonymous/None user -> AttributeError escapes -> a PermissionError handler misses it; the file is preserved
findings.severity_change_reason: Duplicate of security-1 (same root cause); merged and rejected for the same reason
findings.rejection_reason: Duplicate of security-1 (same root cause); merged and rejected for the same reason

findings.rejection_reason: test-strength on correct code: sync.py:17-20 handle these cases, as reviewer probes confirm; the contract's required evidence does not name corrupt-file tests
